clue.text: Novel comment on a successful loft conversion

definitions.meaning: a 1957 novel by John Braine about an ambitious young man climbing the social ladder

definitions.text: comment on a successful loft conversion
definitions.meaning: read literally, a remark about a new bedroom built up under the roof

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on how well a loft conversion has turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: The title of John Braine's novel doubles as a literal description of a converted attic: a bedroom high up in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the book's title and a plain description of a converted attic space.

clue.text: Tries an unusual wine

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters of tries and an are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone samples a wine they have never had before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' tells you to rearrange TRIES and AN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Eyes the symbols of power

definitions.meaning: poetically, eyeballs are called globes or spheres
the jewelled globes held by monarchs at coronations as emblems of sovereignty

explanation.surface: A gaze falls upon the regalia of a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeballs are poetically called by this word, and a sovereign's regalia includes jewelled globes of the same name.

clue.text: A Frenchman concluded that corrections had been made

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, the French form of address for a man
concluded means finished or ended

explanation.surface: A Frenchman ends a session by declaring that the text has been fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A document that has had corrections made to it has been revised.

clue.text: Art movement Italian leader cast aspersions on

indicators.note: movement implies the letters of art shifting position into a new order

parts.note: Il Duce was the title taken by Mussolini as Italy's leader

explanation.surface: An Italian dictator sneers at an artistic school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like part of 'Art movement' (a school of art) but signals an anagram of ART, giving TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander someone is to speak maliciously of them, damaging their reputation.

clue.text: English anger towards Ireland

parts.note: a literary three-letter word for wrath or fury

explanation.surface: An Englishman's rage is directed at the Irish.
explanation.definitionFit: Éire is the Irish-language name of the country.

clue.text: Unconventional fellow not even going to a dance

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An eccentric man shows up at a ball without a matching partner.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric person who behaves strangely is often called this informally.

clue.text: Substitute piano inserted as a last resort

indicators.note: to substitute is to swap things around, here the letters of piano and inserted are exchanged into a new order

explanation.surface: A replacement piano is brought in when all else has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitute' signals an anagram of PIANO INSERTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting out of despair is what one does when every other option has run out.

clue.text: Literary essays in French

parts.note: a French phrase, literally 'fine letters', borrowed into English for light literary writing such as essays

explanation.surface: A collection of essays written in French.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means 'beautiful letters' and is used in English for elegant literary writing.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term for refined literature, especially essays and criticism, is used unchanged in English.

clue.text: The board's absence is significant

parts.note: no means none, an absence of something
a board is a table, as in 'bed and board'

explanation.surface: Missing board members make for a remarkable meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remarkable or worthy of note is significant.

clue.text: Contract to build a viaduct

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to shorten or condense a text
split into two words, a viaduct is a type of bridge spanning a valley

explanation.surface: A contractor is engaged to construct a viaduct.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words for the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a book is to condense it; and a viaduct is a kind of span over a valley.

clue.text: It's wicked to make a quick volte-face

indicators.note: a volte-face is an about-turn, so the word for quick is turned round to face the other way

parts.note: quick in its old sense means living, as in 'the quick and the dead'

explanation.surface: Doing a sudden U-turn is condemned as wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' is in the archaic sense of alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked and sinful behaviour is morally bad.

clue.text: Nothing austere in a perfume

parts.note: the letter O stands for zero or nothing
dour means severe, stern or austere

explanation.surface: An austere person wears no perfume at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfume is a scent or smell.

clue.text: Letters delivered from Lima

indicators.note: the answer is freed or set loose from the letters of Lima in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Correspondence arrives from the Peruvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered from' signals an anagram of LIMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters sent by post are collectively called the post.

clue.text: Within a month Dad is in the Far East

indicators.note: within tells you the word for dad goes inside the word for the month

parts.note: Jan is the abbreviation for January
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Father will be in the Orient within the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is an island nation of East Asia, part of the region called the Far East.

clue.text: Virginia gets heartily sick of the house

indicators.note: heartily suggests going into the heart of the other word, so the word for sick sits in the middle

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia is thoroughly fed up with her home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartily sick of' reads as an idiom for fed up, but 'heartily' puts ILL into the heart of VA.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country or suburban house.

clue.text: The poster returns a Swiss mountain holiday greeting

indicators.note: returns means the mountain's name comes back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain in Switzerland
a card is sent to greet friends at Christmas and other holidays

explanation.surface: A notice about an Alpine holiday is returned along with a greetings card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The poster' looks like the person posting something, but it is the noun: a printed notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a large printed notice displayed in public.

clue.text: Stay back with Leslie to have some food

indicators.note: back means the word for stay is read from the end towards the start

parts.note: to bide is to wait or stay
Les is the short form of the name Leslie

explanation.surface: A guest stays on with Leslie for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay back' reads as an instruction to keep away, but 'Stay' gives the word and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Edibles are things fit to be eaten.

clue.text: Law-and-order measure requires diplomacy by Brazilian city

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city usually called Rio
tact is skill in dealing with people diplomatically

explanation.surface: Keeping order in Rio de Janeiro calls for diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was an 18th-century British law; 'reading the riot act' means a stern warning to restore order.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1714 British statute empowered officials to disperse unruly crowds, keeping public order.

clue.text: Outside broadcast Panorama considers unfit for transmission

parts.note: OB is the broadcasting abbreviation for outside broadcast
a panorama is a wide view or scene

explanation.surface: The BBC's Panorama programme decides some outside footage is too explicit to air.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is a long-running BBC current-affairs programme, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent or lewd material would be banned from the airwaves as offensive.

clue.text: The first half of this should be considered

indicators.note: takes the first two of the four letters of the next word

parts.note: ought means should, as in 'you ought to go'

explanation.surface: A thinker insists the opening half of something deserves careful thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Considered means reflected upon or pondered, as a past participle of think.

clue.text: Open-handed friends

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Friends who are generous with one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open-handed' looks like generous but means shaped like an open hand, a term used of leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a palmate leaf has lobes spreading from one point like fingers of a hand.

clue.text: Station Ernest by the back door

parts.note: a post is a station, as in a sentry's post
Ern is a familiar short form of Ernest

explanation.surface: Ernest is posted to guard the rear entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small rear or side gate, especially in a castle wall.

clue.text: Droll acknowledgement of personal exploitation

definitions.meaning: droll means funny in an odd or wry way
split into two words, a person's admission that they are taking advantage of someone

explanation.surface: Someone wryly admits to taking advantage of others.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as AM USING, what someone exploiting others might confess.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means comical or entertaining; and someone confessing exploitation might say 'I am using you'.

clue.text: Hardy girl suffers small setback

indicators.note: the second half of the word setback tells the solver to read the small-plus-set pair backwards

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
set is taken from the first half of setback as it stands

explanation.surface: A girl named Hardy has a minor reversal of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'setback' into SET and 'back': S plus SET, read backwards, gives the heroine of Thomas Hardy's novel Tess of the d'Urbervilles.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy's tragic heroine in Tess of the d'Urbervilles is the girl named here.

clue.text: Son enters model police force

indicators.note: the letter for son goes into the word for model, entering it

parts.note: to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: A son joins a model police unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a body of men summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law.

clue.text: Broke the chest

definitions.meaning: slang for penniless, out of money
the upper front of the body, especially a woman's breasts

explanation.surface: Someone smashed the treasure chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for bankrupt or penniless, and also the human torso or bosom.

clue.text: Health food council

definitions.meaning: a controlled regime of eating for health
a legislative assembly, such as the Japanese parliament or the imperial assembly of the Holy Roman Empire

explanation.surface: A local council promotes healthy eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen of eating, and also a formal legislative assembly, as in the Diet of Worms.

clue.text: Educated doughboy who travelled to Bethlehem

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a degree held by an educated person
doughboy was slang for an American infantryman, like GI

explanation.surface: A well-educated American soldier made the journey to Bethlehem.
explanation.walkthrough: A doughboy is a First World War American soldier, the same as a GI.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men from the East travelled to Bethlehem to visit the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Opportunity for making an entrance

definitions.meaning: a chance or vacancy, as in a job going
a gap or aperture through which one can go in

explanation.surface: A chance to make a grand entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacancy or chance, and also a gap or doorway through which to pass.

clue.text: Look into the origin of mineral ore

definitions.meaning: split as three words, '...', meaning from a mine, which is where ore comes from

explanation.surface: Investigators study where mineral ore comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as EX A MINE, 'out of a mine', which is where ore originates.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect closely is to look into something; and ore comes 'ex a mine', out of a pit.

clue.text: There is a Socialist candidate completely outpaced

definitions.meaning: read as left-wing plus a person running in an election
beaten so badly in a race that others seem to stand still by comparison

explanation.surface: A Labour candidate is trounced at the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: Left means left-wing and standing means running for election; the phrase also means far outstripped in a race.
